# Engineering Knowledge Base

> Free, beginner-friendly guides to AI engineering, computer science fundamentals, Docker and Kubernetes, and graph machine learning. Every page explains ideas in plain words, works examples by hand, and links to in-browser interactive labs. Written and maintained by Mohammed Saqlain (https://github.com/saqlain2204).

Content is plain HTML with no paywall or login. Citations with a link to the page are welcome. Full page list: https://engineering.msaqlain.com/sitemap.xml

## Start here

- [AI Engineering](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/ai-engineering.html): Learn AI engineering end to end: ML basics, LLMs, training, retrieval, inference, deployment, and agents, with worked examples and labs.
- [CS Fundamentals](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/CS-Fundamentals/cs-fundamentals.html): Core computer science for engineers: operating systems, databases, and computer networks, explained from zero with worked examples and real-world scenarios.
- [Docker & Kubernetes](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/docker-kubernetes.html): From container basics to production Kubernetes: Docker, Compose, cluster architecture, networking, storage, security, scheduling, debugging, and DevOps.
- [Graph Machine Learning](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/graph-ml.html): From zero to expert on Graph Neural Networks - with math derivations, intuition, code, papers, and how GNNs fit with LLMs.
- [Interactive Labs: Learn AI, OS and Networking by Playing](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/index.html): Free interactive labs that run in your browser: self-attention, LLM sampling, CPU scheduling, page replacement, load balancing and subnetting. Move a slider, see the idea.
- [Engineering Knowledge Base: Free Guides to AI, Kubernetes and CS Fundamentals](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/): Free, beginner-friendly guides to AI engineering, LLMs, Docker and Kubernetes, operating systems, databases, networks and graph ML, with worked examples, diagrams and interactive labs.

## Interactive labs

- [Self-Attention Lab: Step Through Q, K, V and Softmax](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/attention.html): Interactive self-attention lab. Pick a token and step through query-key scores, scaling by the square root of d, the causal mask, softmax and the weighted sum of values, with a live attention heatmap.
- [CPU Scheduling Simulator: FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Round Robin, Priority](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/cpu-scheduling.html): Interactive CPU scheduling simulator. Edit processes, pick FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Round Robin or Priority, and get a Gantt chart with waiting, turnaround and response times, plus a side-by-side comparison.
- [Load Balancing Simulator: Round Robin vs Least Connections vs Power of Two](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/load-balancing.html): Interactive load balancer simulator. Add a slow server, raise the load, and compare round robin, random, least connections and power of two choices on p50, p95 and p99 latency.
- [Page Replacement Lab: FIFO vs LRU vs OPT, Step by Step](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/page-replacement.html): Interactive page replacement lab. Step through a reference string with FIFO, LRU and OPT side by side, see every hit and page fault, and find Belady's anomaly yourself.
- [LLM Sampling Lab: Temperature, Top-k, Top-p and Min-p](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/sampling.html): Interactive LLM decoding lab. Move the temperature, top-k, top-p and min-p sliders and watch which next tokens survive, how the probabilities change, and what gets sampled.
- [Subnet Calculator Lab: CIDR, Masks and Bits Explained](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Interactive%20Labs/subnet-calculator.html): Interactive subnet calculator that shows its work. Type an IPv4 address and prefix to see the network, broadcast, host range and mask, bit by bit, and split a network into smaller subnets.

- [Distributed Training](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/learn/Training-Pipeline/ai-engineering-distributed-training.html): Parallelism strategies, memory optimizations, communication systems, and cluster design for training models that do not fit - in memory or in time - on one GPU.

- [Post-Training](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/learn/Training-Pipeline/ai-engineering-post-training.html): Shaping model behavior after SFT using human preferences, reward models, and direct preference optimization.
- [Pretraining](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/learn/Training-Pipeline/ai-engineering-pretraining.html): Building base model capability from raw corpora through next-token prediction at scale - architecture, data, optimization, distributed systems, and scaling laws in full technical depth.

## Research and books

- [Attention Is All You Need](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/research/attention-is-all-you-need.html): The definitive deep-dive into the 2017 paper by Vaswani et al. that introduced the Transformer architecture.
- [Post-Training Mastery | AI Engineering Research](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/research/post-training-mastery.html): Post-Training Mastery - a book on RLHF, DPO, alignment, and modern LLM post-training by Mohammed Saqlain.
- [AI Engineering Research](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/AI%20Engineer/research/research-hub.html): Paper breakdowns and book-length references for deep study.
- [Papers Hub](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/research/papers-hub.html): Organized index of landmark and recent papers. Read the learn notes first, then dive into primary sources.

- [Helm & Observability](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-helm-observability.html): Helm charts, releases, values, Prometheus, Grafana, logging, tracing, and resource quotas for Kubernetes.
- [Kubernetes Networking & Services](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-networking.html): Kubernetes networking: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, Ingress, DNS, Network Policies, CNI, and service meshes.
- [Operators & Custom Resources](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-operators-crds.html): Kubernetes operators from zero: what a controller is, the reconcile loop, watches, informers and work queues, level vs edge triggering, writing a CustomResourceDefinition with a schema, status and printer columns, a toy...
- [Scheduling: Taints, Affinity, Spreading & Priority](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-scheduling.html): How Kubernetes decides which node runs each pod, from zero with worked numbers: allocatable vs capacity, the filter and score phases with a scoring example, nodeSelector and node affinity, taints and tolerations...
- [Kubernetes Storage](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-storage.html): Kubernetes storage: Volumes, PersistentVolumes, PVCs, StorageClasses, CSI drivers, and StatefulSet storage patterns.
- [Debugging Pods: Pending, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-troubleshooting.html): A beginner's playbook for broken Kubernetes pods: the pod lifecycle and where each failure appears, the five commands that solve most cases, Pending, ContainerCreating, ErrImagePull and ImagePullBackOff...
- [Kubernetes Workloads](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/Kubernetes/kubernetes-workloads.html): Kubernetes workloads: Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, CronJobs, probes, HPA, and resource limits.
- [Learn](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Docker-Kubernetes/learn/docker-kubernetes-learn.html): Docker and Kubernetes learning track: fundamentals, Compose, advanced builds, cluster architecture, workloads, scheduling, probes, rollouts and autoscaling, networking, storage, security, Helm, observability, GPU...

## Graph Machine Learning

- [GNN Formula Sheet](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/formulas/graph-ml-formulas.html): All key equations in one place for quick revision.
- [Deep GNNs & Limitations](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Advanced/graph-ml-deep-gnns-limitations.html): Oversmoothing, over-squashing, expressiveness limits, and the fixes that let you go deeper.
- [Graph Transformers](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Advanced/graph-ml-graph-transformers.html): Global attention on graphs - Graphormer, GPS, positional encodings, and when they beat message passing.
- [Heterogeneous Graphs](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Advanced/graph-ml-heterogeneous-graphs.html): Multiple node and edge types, metapaths, R-GCN, HGT, and link prediction on knowledge graphs.
- [Temporal & Dynamic Graphs](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Advanced/graph-ml-temporal-dynamic-graphs.html): Graphs that change over time - snapshots, continuous-time models, and temporal link prediction.
- [Classic GNN Architectures](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Core/graph-ml-classic-architectures.html): GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, GIN, and MPNN - the models you must understand cold. Math, intuition, code, and when to use each.
- [Message Passing Framework](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Core/graph-ml-message-passing.html): The single idea behind almost every GNN: nodes send messages along edges, aggregate them, and update themselves.
- [Spectral Methods](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Core/graph-ml-spectral-methods.html): Where GCN really comes from - graph Fourier transform, spectral convolution, ChebNet, and why spatial methods won in practice.
- [Graph Foundations](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Foundations/graph-ml-foundations.html): Graph ML from zero: what graphs are, adjacency matrix, Laplacian, graph tasks, homophily, and why relational data needs special models.
- [Representation & Data Preparation](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Foundations/graph-ml-representation-data.html): How to turn raw data into a graph, engineer features, split correctly, and load into PyTorch Geometric - without leaking labels.
- [GNNs in the LLM Era](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Practice/graph-ml-gnns-and-llms.html): How graph neural networks and large language models work together - and when each wins alone.
- [Recent Advances & Papers](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Practice/graph-ml-recent-advances-papers.html): Landmark papers, 2020–2026 trends, theses to read, code repos, and open problems.
- [Training & Scaling](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Practice/graph-ml-training-scaling.html): Losses, sampling, mini-batch training on billion-edge graphs, and debugging GNN training.
- [When to Use GNNs & Evaluation](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/Practice/graph-ml-when-to-use-evaluation.html): Honest decision guide - GNN vs tabular ML vs LLM, metrics, baselines, and common evaluation mistakes.
- [Graph ML Learn](https://engineering.msaqlain.com/Graph%20ML/learn/graph-ml-learn.html): Complete learning path for Graph Machine Learning and Graph Neural Networks - from basics to expert level.
